result.note: Tests the April 2026 change of NITI Aayog vice-chairman, the body's recommatory status compared with the Planning Commission, and features of the new roster.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, who replaced Suman Bery as vice-chairman of NITI Aayog?
questions.explain: Former Chief Economic Adviser Ashok Lahiri took over as vice-chairman on 24 April 2026. Rajiv Gauba, K V Raju and Abhay Karandikar were named full-time members in the same overhaul.
questions.source: On April 24, former Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) Ashok Lahiri replaced Suman Bery as vice-chairman.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
items: It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
Like the Planning Commission, it controls plan funds and has allocation leverage over states.
It has no statutory authority and no enforcement power.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Plan funds and allocation leverage over states belonged to the Planning Commission, while NITI Aayog is purely recommendatory with no budget. Several opposition-ruled states already boycott its meetings.
questions.source: NITI Aayog is purely recommendatory, with no budget, no statutory authority, and no enforcement power.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog overhaul completed in April–May 2026:
items: The new vice-chairman is the first to hold the post with elected political experience.
Former Cabinet Secretary Rajiv Gauba was the only full-time member retained from the earlier team.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Ashok Lahiri is a BJP legislator from Balurghat in West Bengal, and Gauba was the only holdover among the full-time members. Two more members joined on 2 May 2026, taking total membership to seven.
questions.source: Lahiri, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislator from West Bengal's Balurghat, is the first vice-chairman with elected political experience.
